overview: This Senate resolution commemorates June 19, 2025, as Juneteenth National Independence Day. Juneteenth marks June 19, 1865, when Union soldiers arrived in Galveston, Texas, with news that the Civil War was over and enslaved people were free, more than two and a half years after the Emancipation Proclamation. The resolution recounts how the day began as a celebration in Texas and is now a federal holiday observed in every state. It recognizes the day's historical importance and supports continued nationwide celebrations as a chance for Americans to learn about the country's past. The Senate agreed to it on June 25, 2025.
for: Supporters say it honors the end of slavery and encourages Americans to learn about an important chapter of the nation's history.
against: Critics say it is symbolic and does not change any law or spending, since Juneteenth is already a federal holiday.
